items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Bechet and myself, we was more than Tumpman... I was in a four piece band up in the hole in the walls... And Bechet and Johnny. And Dots, myself, Charlie.

ctx.x: Before they started making records, who could play good blues?

Well, as far as I can say, Bechet and myself, we was more than Tumpman. What do we call it? Tumpman. I was in a four piece band up in the hole in the walls and there, you know. A lot of the fast women. Couldn't play nothing but the blues. Short bands. Yeah. Short bands. He played in the sense of running and it wasn't doing nothing. And Bechet and Johnny. And Dots, myself, Charlie. Charlie. Yeah, Charlie. Blind Charlie. Blind Charlie, yeah. Yeah. Who else was he? Kaiser. Kaiser? Kaiser? He was on. Yeah. That's…
You mean the district? Yeah. Yeah. I was in the district. I was in the district. I was in the district. And all the place.
